author: WP01
summary: Introduces CNA as a C++ reimplementation of XNA 4.0: a translation target rather than a loader, three engineering problems (API, runtime, GPU), the README's goals, the evidence-vector stance, the negative space, verification instruments (FNA harness, Windows 7 reproducer, strict check, oracle), the Song/FNA case, the release and phase model, and the Ms-PL licence. Updated for d6e9ff05 but partly stale: it still says CNA has no content builder or reader bootstrap and overstates the strict check. The site had the version model, oracle and negative space in pieces; the translation-target framing, authority split, Song case, goals and licence detail were missing and now form the CNA and XNA 4.0 page.

empty_sections.heading: CNA and XNA 4.0
empty_sections.reason: chapter title; every section below it is recorded

concepts.text: CNA is a native C++ reimplementation of the XNA 4.0 programming model built as C++23; SDL3 is the default platform and audio implementation but those are independent axes, and rendering goes through 25 public identities over 21 families, one of which a multi-renderer build selects at run time.
tokens: 25 public renderer identities over 21 implementation families
SDL3 is the default for both

concepts.text: CNA is a translation target, not a loader or binary compatibility layer: it cannot run a C# assembly, porting translates source, and a property access becomes getXProperty()/setXProperty(); names and observable contracts stay XNA-shaped while language and ownership model cannot.
tokens: cannot run an existing XNA game

target.evidence: CLAUDE.md (C# Properties); no CLR in tree

concepts.text: Reproducing the API means XNA's public namespaces, class names, signatures and observable behaviour must exist in C++ so XNA or FNA code has somewhere to land.

Reproducing the runtime means supplying the .NET vocabulary XNA assumes (Object, events, exceptions, TimeSpan, collections) through the sibling sharp-runtime, a deliberately partial C++ subset of the .NET class library rather than a CLR.
tokens: without attempting to implement a CLR

concepts.text: Reproducing the GPU means the same GraphicsDevice/SpriteBatch/Effect surface must produce pixels on very different back ends (SDL's 2D renderer, EasyGL, Vulkan, WebGPU, Direct3D 9/11/12, browser canvas and DOM, a DirectDraw reimplementation); identical API presence does not imply identical behaviour or evidence.
tokens: Identical API presence does not imply identical behaviour

target.evidence: cmake/RendererIdentities.cmake; the Direct3D renderers are Windows renderers exercised mostly through Wine, not renderers that exist 'under Wine'

concepts.text: CNA's README (quoted from a July 2026 snapshot) describes CNA as a C++ reimplementation of XNA 4.0 built on SDL3 and a pluggable renderer layer, a framework/runtime and abstraction layer and not a game.

target.evidence: README.md at 009d40f5 still says 'built on SDL3'; CLAUDE.md now says 'a CNA-owned platform abstraction (SDL3 is the default implementation)', and native X11/Wayland/Win32 platforms avoid SDL

concepts.text: XNA Game Studio was Microsoft's managed game framework; Microsoft discontinued it and the community responded with FNA (and MonoGame).
The pinned local FNA reference selects its SDL3 platform by default and keeps SDL2 only through FNA_PLATFORM_BACKEND=SDL2, so calling FNA an SDL2 runtime is historical shorthand.
CNA asks a different question from FNA (what if the code does not have to be C#?), offering a native C++ path without a managed runtime for teams that like the XNA/MonoGame model.
tokens: what if the code does not have to be C#?

concepts.text: CNA is also meant as a target for porting existing XNA games, with the Speedy Blupi and Planet Blupi ports (via free-direct) as worked examples.
concepts.note: The Blupi material belongs to the ecosystem map; the case study itself is another package's unit.

target.evidence: cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (free-eggbert/planetblupi consume free-direct); mobile-eggbert is the CNA port

concepts.text: At TARGET CNA has a modular framework, independent platform and audio, a C ABI at 0.29.0, 25 identities, XNB read/write, CNB/CNJ, a build-time pipeline, a glTF importer and real media types; that establishes breadth, not uniform parity.
tokens: source-level, not built by any CI job

target.evidence: The chapter calls the C API 'buildable'; no CI job builds it and a build was not verified (docs/verification.html#ci)

concepts.section: Design goals, in the project's own words
concepts.text: CNA's README lists six goals: recreate the XNA experience in native C++; a native path for teams needing non-managed toolchain control; mirror XNA namespaces incrementally; decouple gameplay API from renderers; one API across rendering technologies; keep SDL/OpenGL/Vulkan concerns behind abstractions.
tokens: keep SDL, OpenGL and Vulkan-level concerns behind framework abstractions

concepts.section: Design goals, in the project's own words
concepts.text: The middle goals are one idea, the renderer abstraction, realised concretely as the IGraphicsRenderer contract.

concepts.section: Verification is a vector, not a leaderboard
concepts.text: There is no one-number answer to how tested CNA is: a test definition may be unregistered in a build, CTest may register a command the host cannot run, a renderer may succeed without consuming effect state, and a correct pixel on one translated runtime does not prove another host.
tokens: A claim is a vector, not a score

concepts.section: Verification is a vector, not a leaderboard
concepts.text: A claim is recorded as a vector: identity and family, configuration, execution host, driver or translation layer, oracle, and unavailable branches.

concepts.section: Verification is a vector, not a leaderboard
concepts.text: Examples occupy different tiers: the 25/21 registry is structural evidence only; the DIRECTX9 corpus compares with real XNA but through Wine and DXVK; HTML_DOM has executed Chromium evidence while another web identity's build proves less; campaign pass fractions belong to their campaigns.
CNA is not a game: it ships no flagship demo but a test suite and minimal verification executables such as hello-triangle-sdl.

target.evidence: README.md ('not a game') confirmed; hello-triangle-sdl is easy-gl's example (easy-gl@deda7a42 README), not a CNA program

concepts.text: CNA is described as not an XNA content builder: no MGCB-style import/process/write toolchain and no automatic reader bootstrap, so a game must register the built-in readers before loading XNB.
concepts.note: Both halves are false at TARGET: a build-time pipeline exists and Game registers the 61 built-in readers itself.

concepts.text: CNA is not universally compiled-shader compatible: stock effects, compiled D3D9 Effect Framework bytecode through the public Effect constructor on qualified renderers, and renderer-specific ShaderEffect are separate routes; .fx/HLSL source, DXBC and MGFX are different formats.
GamerServices reimplements the API shape with local semantics and no real Xbox Live, matching how FNA handles the namespace.

target.evidence: CNA persists achievements/leaderboards and draws real Guide overlays where FNA keeps no-op stubs; 'matching FNA' is wrong for the local half

concepts.text: CNA is not a drop-in DirectX runtime: free-direct implements a game-driven DirectDraw/DirectSound/DirectPlay subset over SDL3 whose default DirectPlay transport is in-process and whose ENet transport speaks only to the same reimplementation.
Differential testing runs a genuine FNA.dll (tools/fna-reference) and compares CNA's behaviour with it rather than with a written description of FNA.
Disputed behaviour that FNA differential testing cannot settle is checked against real XNA 4.0 in a Windows 7 virtual machine.

target.evidence: docs/xna_culling_compatibility_audit.md (CullMode reproducer run by the owner on a Windows 7/XNA 4.0 VM)

concepts.text: CNA_STRICT_XNA_API, checked by two standalone CMake targets, is said to give a mechanical guarantee that the public Microsoft::Xna::Framework surface has not silently grown project-specific extensions.
concepts.note: Overclaim: the harness proves the mechanism for the Devices/Sensors slice only; it guarantees nothing about the graphics, content or input surface.

target.evidence: cmake/Harnesses.cmake: both targets compile only tools/devices/StrictXnaApiSurface*Check.cpp over the Microsoft::Devices/Sensors surface; marker completeness elsewhere is not checked

concepts.text: The DIRECTX9 renderer has an oracle corpus diffing CNA's render against the real XNA 4.0 runtime's render of the same declarative scenes; its registered gate runs the whole corpus at tolerance zero, and a pass count still needs an identified run.

FNA is authoritative for behaviour but Microsoft's reference assemblies for API surface: FNA's Song.cs omits Album, Artist, Genre and ToString(), eight FNA-based review rounds missed it, a member-level diff against the Microsoft XML found it, and CNA added non-owning back-pointers filled by MediaLibrary (nullptr outside a library).

target.evidence: CHECKLIST.md (API surface section, MEDIA-174/180); modules/media/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Media/Song.hpp; FNA@b3551247 src/Media/Song.cs has no Album/Artist/Genre

concepts.text: The checklist's lesson is that 'FNA doesn't have it either' is not a justification; since 2026-09-04 measured XNA also wins over FNA on behaviour.

target.evidence: CHECKLIST.md; CLAUDE.md (Where FNA and XNA disagree)

concepts.text: Where the book states a behaviour as fact it rests on the project's tests, documents or source comments, and dated snapshots or estimates keep their qualification.
concepts.note: Book editorial stance; the site states its own evidence basis per page.

concepts.section: The first tagged release and the continuing phase workflow
concepts.text: On 2026-08-20 the annotated tag v0.1.0-alpha.1 established the first Semantic Versioning release.

concepts.section: The first tagged release and the continuing phase workflow
concepts.text: CNA developed continuously from 2025-02-22 without conventional releases, with numbered phases and tasks carrying engineering state.
concepts.note: Chronology (first commit da77b5c55 is dated 2025-02-22); not current technical documentation.

concepts.section: The first tagged release and the continuing phase workflow
concepts.text: The product version is assembled from CMake's numeric 0.1.0 project version and a separate alpha.1 pre-release field; cmake/Version.cmake generates CNA/Version.hpp, and the tag spelling carries the leading v.

concepts.section: The first tagged release and the continuing phase workflow
concepts.text: Before 1.0 the release policy permits breaking changes when the minor or pre-release version advances; the C ABI (0.29.0) versions separately, and the tree still reporting alpha.1 does not make TARGET the tagged release.

concepts.section: The first tagged release and the continuing phase workflow
concepts.text: Numbered phases and tasks in the plan files still carry bounded work alongside tags, and a closing count is a snapshot of one configuration, never combined with current source, registration or oracle totals.
tokens: closing count is a snapshot of one configuration

concepts.text: CNA is licensed under the Ms-PL like FNA because portions are derived from FNA, most visibly the Direct3D 9 renderer's vendored Stock Effects HLSL.

The Ms-PL permits commercial use, modification and redistribution, includes a contributor patent grant and a patent-retaliation termination clause, and is not a copyleft that reaches a separate game built against CNA.
concepts.note: Stated on the page as a reading of the licence text, not legal advice.
